subject: Civil Engineering
title: Soil Compaction: Packing It Tight
description: A micro-lesson that makes Soil Compaction: Packing It Tight usable.

hook.text: Loose soil settles over time. Buildings on loose soil crack and tilt.

buildup.text: Compaction forces air out of soil, pushing grains closer together.

discovery.text: The Proctor test finds the optimal moisture content — too dry or too wet won't compact.

twist.text: Heavy rollers compact roads. Vibratory plates compact sand. Each soil needs its method.

climax.text: Nuclear density gauges measure compaction on-site in seconds — instant quality control.

punchline.text: Good compaction prevents settlement before it starts.

quiz.question: What does the Proctor test determine?
options: The chemical composition of the soil
The optimal moisture content for maximum compaction density
The depth of the water table below the surface
